summary.tldr: Requires the federal minister to develop a national framework to align skilled trades certification and make it easier to move across provinces.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Employment and Social Development to develop a national framework that reduces barriers for skilled trades workers by modernising, streamlining and harmonising certification and credentials across Canada.
Requires at least nine months of consultations with provinces, trades regulators, employers, unions, apprenticeship groups, Indigenous bodies, and training and education institutions.
Requires the framework to list skilled trades across Canada and compare provincial standards and credentials to map where they match.

Requires measures to harmonise standards, cut duplicate steps, streamline recognition from one province to another, support updated certification for new technologies and trades, and promote public awareness of skilled trades.
Requires the Minister to table a report within one year, then annual progress reports, and publish each report online.
Requires a parliamentary review within five years, with a report that may recommend changes to the framework.
summary.background: The bill defines a skilled trade as a trade that is certified or regulated by a province, including trades with Red Seal or Blue Seal credentials. It gives the Minister of Employment and Social Development responsibility for the framework.
